paper_title: Constraints on scalar field dark matter from co-located Michelson interferometers
coupling_convention: d_e (dimensionless coupling to photons, constraining fine-structure constant variation)
notes: Paper constrains scalar field DM coupling to photons (Λγ) and electrons (Λe) using the Fermilab Holometer twin interferometer. The coupling parameters Λγ and Λe are inverse energy scales (dimensions of GeV^-1) that parameterize the interaction term φ/Λγ · FμνF^μν in the Lagrangian. Figure 2 shows exclusion limits as functions of DM mass mφ for three scenarios: Basic Scalar (ρ=0.4 GeV/cm³), Dilaton/Modulus, and Relaxion Halo. The paper reports constraints in the mass range 1.6×10^-12 to 1.0×10^-7 eV at 95% CL. However, extracting precise numerical coupling values from Figure 2 is difficult due to figure resolution and logarithmic axes. The data_points provided represent the mass range boundaries with a placeholder coupling value (1e5 GeV^-1 is approximate and should be read from the figure). The coupling type is ScalarPhoton because the paper explicitly constrains variation of the fine-structure constant α through the photon coupling term φ/Λγ · FμνF^μν, which is the defining characteristic of ScalarPhoton. The paper also constrains ScalarElectron (electron mass variation via Λe), but the primary physics and most prominent results concern photon coupling.
